summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — TPL +10%, MRNA +7%, SNDK +7%, FDXF +6%, INCY +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (LITE -9%, GPN -8%, CHTR -8%, NOW -8%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: TPL (+9.69%)

top_movers.catalyst: 5-year KEYNOTE-942 follow-up data presented at ASCO 2026 showed mRNA-4157/V940 + KEYTRUDA reduced melanoma recurrence/death by 49% (HR 0.51), sustaining and extending prior efficacy readouts.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. MRNA is a high-beta biotech whose moves are driven by binary clinical-data events (ASCO presentations, FDA decisions); quant universes typically exclude it via biotech carve-outs, volatility caps, or gap-risk filters given its history of >50% single-day swings on trial data.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a clinical-conference catalyst gate: monitor ASCO/ESMO abstract release dates and, on confirmed positive oncology data prints, allow a 1-session momentum entry for names with gap ≥+5% and volume ≥2× 30-day avg, gated by a market-cap floor (e.g. ≥$10B) to control binary risk.

top_movers.catalyst: Morgan Stanley raised SNDK price target 59% to $1,750 (Overweight) and Barclays upgraded to Overweight on the same day; CounterPoint Research published AI-driven NAND demand analysis amplifying the move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SNDK is a large-cap NAND memory name (~$280B implied cap) not yet added to any screener. The +6.7% move was analyst-upgrade-driven and intraday: dual PT raise/upgrade catalyst is not capturable by post-open momentum or mean-reversion signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a news-catalyst universe gate: names receiving ≥2 major-bank upgrades or PT raises ≥30% on the same day should be auto-enrolled in the momentum strategy for that session, with a first entry permitted within 20 min of open and an intraday stop at –2%.

top_movers.catalyst: FedEx Freight completed its spinoff from FDX on 2026-06-01 and began NYSE trading; a wave of analyst initiations on/around June 4 (Wolfe Research $180, BofA $185, Evercore $168 — all Outperform/Buy) drove the post-spinoff re-rating.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — FDXF has only 3 days of price history (listed 2026-06-01), so it cannot satisfy any minimum-history requirement for momentum or mean-reversion signals and was never seeded into any strategy's tradable universe.
top_movers.suggestion: Create a spinoff-watch list that auto-enrolls freshly listed spinoffs in the news-reactive strategy on day 1, waiving the minimum-history filter but capping position size at 50% of normal until 20 sessions of history accumulate.

top_movers.catalyst: Phase 3 frontMIND ASCO data (tafasitamab + R-CHOP cut first-line DLBCL progression/death risk 25%) presented May 30; BofA and Stifel raised PTs to $124/$123 on Jun 3–4, sparking a post-conference analyst repricing rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. INCY is a large-cap biopharma (~$20B market cap) whose move was ASCO-readout driven with analyst PT hikes landing 2 sessions post-conference — quant entry signals structurally lag such catalyst-driven biotech repricing by design.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a clinical-catalyst overlay: auto-include S&P 500 biopharma names with confirmed ASCO/EHA plenary slots; enable a news-reactive entry gate within 2 sessions of a ≥$3 analyst PT upgrade post-readout, provided intraday gap at trigger is ≤+8%.

top_movers.catalyst: UBS raised URI price target to $1,145 from $1,025 (maintaining Buy), citing H2 2026 construction recovery in manufacturing, data centers, and power; easing 10-year yield to 4.46% amplified the move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — URI is a large-cap US equipment rental name (~$1,057/share). The +6% move was analyst-upgrade-driven; without pre-market broker research ingestion, no signal existed before price action materialized.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sell-side upgrade scanner: flag names with a tier-1 broker price-target raise ≥+10% confirmed by pre-market volume ≥1.3× 30-day avg, then gate entry at the first 15-min candle close above the gap-up open.

top_movers.catalyst: Profit-taking selloff after LITE surged ~14% the prior session on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Computex commentary highlighting AI optical-networking demand; no new company-specific negative news.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. LITE ($938, +140% YTD) is a high-cap AI-photonics name; the -8.86% was a pure mean-reversion after a +14% prior-day sector-sentiment surge, requiring pre-existing long exposure or short capability to trade.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a prior-day momentum fade rule: names with D-1 gain ≥+10% on sector sentiment (not earnings), RSI ≥80, and ADV ≥$300M qualify for a next-session short-fade signal — requires enabling the short-selling module first.

top_movers.catalyst: Susquehanna cut GPN price target $119→$111 on June 3, flagging a more cautious travel-revenue exposure view and trimming FY2026 growth est. to 4%; stock extended losses ~8% into June 4.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. GPN is a large-cap payments-tech name (GICS 45203020) in a year-long downtrend; the universe gap itself is the miss — no filter ever evaluated it, so no entry or short signal was generated.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change for current long-only strategies; if short capability is added, implement a sell-side trigger: ≥1 PT cut ≥5% on a large-cap fintech name (GICS 4520) opens a short within 30 min of the next market open.

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh catalyst; continued post-Q1-2026 earnings selldown (Apr 25: 120k broadband subs lost, EPS miss, capex +19%) as fiber and FWA competition accelerates; CHTR has fallen ~64% YoY.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. CHTR is a large-cap telecom in prolonged fundamental decline. The drop continues a post-Q1 trend with no fresh catalyst or gap setup; capturing it requires short capability the bot likely lacks.
top_movers.suggestion: (No actionable change — CHTR is outside risk tolerance; the move is a continuation short requiring short capability not currently modeled, and adding large-cap telecom to any existing strategy's universe would break its sector/factor scope.)

top_movers.catalyst: UBS 'Sell' downgrade (cut 2026 cRPO growth est. from 20%→16%, citing Armis integration margin compression + Middle East on-prem deal delays) accelerated a 3-day profit-taking slide after NOW's ~24% post-Q1-earnings surge.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. Even if added, the trade is a multi-session short of an overextended post-earnings gap — requiring short capability the bot does not have; the long-side entry was pre-earnings and outside rule-based signal scope.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change — catching the fade requires shorting a post-earnings overextension; wire a 'faded gap ≥15% + Day 2 close down ≥5% on rising volume' trigger only after short capability is enabled for the enterprise-software universe.
